body:
Closes #8006 (albeit in an unsatisfactory way).

These features are incompatible because they use global cdef variables (which are currently outside the module state). I've already added existing warnings for that feature in user code but the `subinterpreters_compatible` flag doesn't make it into the utility code.

I think the easiest fix is to add a special-cased warning for these two bits of utility code. I've tried to do it in a semi-generic way rather than just checking a hardcoded list of names. I don't think any other Cython utility code should have this problem (although there's undoubtedly bits of global state that I haven't spotted elsewhere).

comment_data.body: Then I'd make it more specific to that use case. Call it `warn_for_subinterpreters()` and call it `if module_scope.directives['subinterpreters_compatible'] != 'no'`. That makes it clear when it can be removed.

commit.message:
Add warnings for subinterpreters for memoryviews and enums

Closes #8006 (albeit in an unsatisfactory way).

These features are incompatible because they use global cdef
variables (which are currently outside the module state). I've
already added existing warnings for that feature in user code
but the `subinterpreters_compatible` flag doesn't make it into
the utility code.

I think the easiest fix is to add a special-cased warning for
these two bits of utility code. I've tried to do it in a
semi-generic way rather than just checking a hardcoded list of
names. I don't think any other Cython utility code should have this
problem (although there's undoubtedly bits of global state
that I haven't spotted elsewhere).
Skip test in shared utility mode
Add an explicit warning for the shared utility build
Fix common case where no warning is given
Make warning work for modules depending on the shared utility
